paragraphs.heading: How do you confirm the card number and check its value?
paragraphs.user_question: How do you confirm the card number and check its value?
paragraphs.increment: 基础答案：Provides a usable identification-to-price sequence rather than one amount for a character. 本段不计为独家或一手发现。
paragraphs.draft:
1. Read the full collector number, including both parts of a slash number.
2. Match the expansion, artwork and language.
3. Match the finish, such as the specific foil treatment, before choosing a price series.
4. Read the source, currency and observation date attached to that reference.
5. Compare the same condition and object type: a loose card, an existing graded copy and a sealed box are different purchases.

page_plans.draft_markdown:
Delta Reign is the Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution expansion released in the United States on November 6, 2026. The source-linked checklist below contains 141 numbered English cards: 103 main-set cards and 38 secret cards, with MEP promos kept separate. Use the full collector number to choose a printing before comparing a price.

## When did Delta Reign come out?

The **Delta Reign release date was November 6, 2026**. The [official launch announcement](https://press.pokemon.com/en/MEDIA-ALERT-Legendary-Pokemon-Mega-Rayquaza-ex-Descends-into-Battle-in) lists booster packs, Elite Trainer Boxes and collections among its products. A shop can still show an old preorder label or a later shipping allocation. Read the current delivery terms for the item you are ordering; the expansion has already launched.

## Delta Reign card list: main set and secret cards

The launch highlights Mega Rayquaza ex, Mega Golurk ex, Mega Malamar ex and Mega Golisopod ex. **Checklist source: [PokéCottage](https://pokecottage.com/sets/delta-reign-card-list); checked November 16, 2026.** The numbered English checklist below has 103 main-set cards and 38 secret cards. Promo cards with MEP numbers are separate from this 001/103–141/103 sequence.

### Which number should I use for Mega Rayquaza ex?

Use the full **/103** number for this English checklist. Mega Rayquaza ex appears at **084/103, 138/103 and 141/103**. During our November 16 source check, the top “most expensive” module on PokéCottage’s English guide displayed **113/076**, while its numbered English list used **/103**. Match the number in the card row, then check language, artwork and finish before comparing amounts.

| What you see | How to use it |
|---|---|
| 084/103 | Select the numbered 084 row in the English checklist |
| 138/103 or 141/103 | Select that exact numbered printing; the price examples keep them separate |
| A result ending /076 | Check its own set and language before comparing it with a /103 card |

### Why does one page show 141 cards and another show 242 items?

The **141-card Delta Reign checklist** and PriceCharting’s **242 catalog items** count different objects. The **141-row checklist** on this page covers the English numbered sequence from **001/103 to 141/103**. PriceCharting’s captured Delta Reign page displayed **242 catalog items** and offered separate filters for sealed products and variants; its visible rows included an Elite Trainer Box and reverse-holo entries alongside numbered cards. Use the numbered checklist to check the main and secret sequence. Use the catalog’s matching item and finish when you compare a specific card or sealed product.

## Is Mega Rayquaza ex the same as an older M Rayquaza-EX?

**No. The expansion and collector number identify the printing.** A search for Delta Reign Rayquaza can also surface older XY cards named M Rayquaza-EX. These catalog records are useful examples of why the number matters:

| Older printing | Expansion | Number and catalog entry |
|---|---|---|
| M Rayquaza EX | XY—Roaring Skies | [61/108](/cards/98097) |
| M Rayquaza EX | XY—Roaring Skies | [76/108](/cards/98112) |
| M Rayquaza EX, Full Art | XY—Roaring Skies | [105/108](/cards/98141) |
| M Rayquaza EX, Shiny Full Art | XY—Ancient Origins | [98/98](/cards/101520) |

A 76/108 card and a 98/98 card are different records even when both depict Rayquaza. Keep their price histories separate. Our [Mega Rayquaza printing guide](/blog/mega-rayquaza-ex-card-values) explains the comparison and links to these existing entries. Use a Delta Reign listing only when its own set, image and full number agree with your copy.

## How do the Legendary Stadium halves work?

A **Legendary Stadium combines two Stadium cards** to form extended artwork and a gameplay feature. Pokémon’s announcement says that a booster containing a Legendary Stadium includes both required halves. This is about the contents of a qualifying pack, not a promise of a Stadium in every pack. When checking a listing, confirm whether the seller is offering a pair or one half.

## Should you buy packs, an Elite Trainer Box or singles?

Choose a product for the experience you want. Packs provide unopened cards. An Elite Trainer Box adds its stated promo and accessories. A single-card listing lets you select the identified printing rather than opening packs to find it. Compare the sale unit, edition and contents before comparing two totals.

| Product | Booster packs | Main bundled extras | Listed US release window |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Booster Display Box | 36 | Pack-focused format | November 6, 2026 |
| Booster Bundle | 6 | Pack-focused format | November 6, 2026 |
| Regular Elite Trainer Box | 9 | 1 full-art foil Kyogre and accessories | November 6, 2026 |
| Pokémon Center Elite Trainer Box | 11 | 2 Kyogre promos; one has the Center logo | November 6, 2026 |
| Build & Battle Box | 4 | 40-card ready-to-play deck including 1 of 4 foil promos | November 20, 2026 for wider availability |

Product contents and listed dates come from the [official product showcase](https://www.pokemon.com/us/news/pokemon-tcg-mega-evolution-delta-reign-product-showcase). Build & Battle’s November 20 wider availability follows earlier prerelease access: the [official expansion page](https://tcg.pokemon.com/en-us/expansions/delta-reign/) lists prerelease events starting October 24. Those dates describe different purchase windows.

The Center edition’s product identifier is **10-10438-112**. Its logo-bearing Kyogre is part of the sealed contents. For dated US offers, membership conditions and box-versus-case comparisons, use the [Delta Reign ETB guide](/blog/delta-reign-etb). A retailer’s asking price and a manufacturer’s MSRP need separate labels; a large case total also needs its box quantity.

## Are the launch retailer promos inside the ETB?

The US launch gift was a separate offer for a qualifying **Pokémon TCG purchase of $15 or more**. It used the **“What’s Your Favorite?” stamp**: Groudon at GameStop, Giratina at Best Buy, and Kyogre at Hot Topic, Five Below, Barnes & Noble and Macy’s. The offer began November 6 while supplies lasted, with participating-retailer terms. [See the US announcement](https://press.pokemon.com/en/MEDIA-ALERT-Legendary-Pokemon-Mega-Rayquaza-ex-Descends-into-Battle-in).

That stamp and the Pokémon Center logo identify different promotions. An ETB’s included Kyogre, a Center-logo Kyogre and a retailer gift should be checked separately. Ask for a clear image of the stamp and confirm whether a listed bonus is included with the purchase. A sealed box’s contents do not establish a store’s remaining gift supply.

## How do you confirm the card number and check its value?

1. Read the full collector number, including both parts of a slash number.
2. Match the expansion, artwork and language.
3. Match the finish, such as the specific foil treatment, before choosing a price series.
4. Read the source, currency and observation date attached to that reference.
5. Compare the same condition and object type: a loose card, an existing graded copy and a sealed box are different purchases.

The [Pokémon catalog](/games/pokemon) and [card search](/cards?game=pokemon&q=Delta%20Reign) are entry points for supported records. CardScanFox’s Delta Reign set currently has no public single-card entries, so use the official material to establish the printing first. A missing catalog row is not a zero value. An older Rayquaza amount does not fill that gap.

For an available record, compare the same price series over time. A large percentage rise can start from a low amount, and a raw reference does not value a graded slab. The [raw-versus-graded guide](/blog/raw-vs-graded-card-values) explains that distinction. Record the printing and source with your comparison so you can check like-for-like amounts later.

## Where can you check Delta Reign pull rates?

For German-language opening estimates, read our [Delta-Herrschaft pull-rate guide](/blog/pokemon-delta-herrschaft-pull-rate). It separates a rarity-tier result from the chance of a particular card and keeps reported samples attributed. Those estimates answer a different question from a checklist or a product’s pack count. A desired single and a box-opening experience are separate buying goals.

paragraphs.question: Which contents should I use when product listings disagree?

For the **Delta Reign ETB**, use the manufacturer’s description for the exact edition. In our November 16 page check, Pokémon’s standard-box showcase listed **40 Energy cards and a plastic coin**. These are different descriptions, so we keep the manufacturer’s standard-box specification in the contents table.

| Field checked | Manufacturer’s standard-box description | Marketplace description captured |
|---|---|---|
| Energy cards | 40 | 45 |
| Play-accessory wording | Plastic coin | Two plastic condition markers |

For the Center edition, Pokémon Center’s **SKU 10-10438-112** separately lists **40 Energy cards, one plastic coin and six dividers**. Apply those itemized counts to that Center product. A seller’s generic accessory paragraph should not select a different edition for your comparison.

page_plans.draft_markdown:
## What comes in a Delta Reign ETB?

A **Delta Reign ETB** comes in two versions: the regular box has **9 booster packs and one full-art foil Kyogre promo**; the Pokémon Center box has **11 packs and two Kyogre promos**, including one with the Center logo. Choose the edition, then compare the purchase quantity and delivered cost.

| Contents | Regular ETB | Pokémon Center ETB |
|---|---|---|
| Delta Reign booster packs | 9 | 11 |
| Full-art foil Kyogre promos | 1 | 2, one bearing the Pokémon Center logo |
| Card sleeves | 65 | 65 |
| Energy cards | 40 | 40 |
| Storage dividers | 6 | 6 |
| Play accessories | 6 damage-counter dice, a coin-flip die and a plastic coin | The same listed quantities |
| Other contents | Player’s guide, storage box and TCG Live code card | Player’s guide, storage box and TCG Live code card |

Pokémon’s showcase supplies the core standard-box contents. GameStop additionally itemizes six damage-counter dice, six dividers and a TCG Live code. The Center edition adds two packs and a logo-bearing promo to the listed bundle. Its official product page identifies it as **SKU 10-10438-112**. That identifier belongs to the Center edition; use the exact title and contents when comparing another store’s regular box. [Read the Pokémon Center contents](https://www.pokemoncenter.com/product/10-10438-112/pokemon-tcg-mega-evolution-delta-reign-pokemon-center-elite-trainer-box) and [GameStop’s regular-box description](https://www.gamestop.com/toys-games/trading-cards/products/pokemon-trading-card-game-delta-reign-elite-trainer-box/20037568.html).

### Which contents should I use when product listings disagree?

For the **Delta Reign ETB**, use the manufacturer’s description for the exact edition. In our November 16 page check, Pokémon’s standard-box showcase listed **40 Energy cards and a plastic coin**. The TCGplayer standard-box description listed **45 Energy cards and two plastic condition markers**. These are different descriptions, so we keep the manufacturer’s standard-box specification in the contents table.

| Field checked | Manufacturer’s standard-box description | Marketplace description captured |
|---|---|---|
| Energy cards | 40 | 45 |
| Play-accessory wording | Plastic coin | Two plastic condition markers |

For the Center edition, Pokémon Center’s **SKU 10-10438-112** separately lists **40 Energy cards, one plastic coin and six dividers**. Apply those itemized counts to that Center product. A seller’s generic accessory paragraph should not select a different edition for your comparison.

## Which Delta Reign ETB promo or stamp do you want?

There are three different promotion types to recognize. The regular ETB includes its Kyogre card. The Center box includes a regular Kyogre promo plus a Kyogre promo carrying the Pokémon Center logo. A seller describing a “stamped promo” should show which stamp is on the card.

The launch also had a separate US retailer gift offer for eligible Pokémon TCG purchases of **$15 or more**. Those cards carried a **“What’s Your Favorite?” stamp**. The official announcement named Groudon at GameStop, Giratina at Best Buy, and Kyogre at several other participating retailers. These gifts were available from November 6 while supplies lasted. A retailer gift is separate from the contents sealed inside an ETB. Check the [official US promotion details](https://press.pokemon.com/en/MEDIA-ALERT-Legendary-Pokemon-Mega-Rayquaza-ex-Descends-into-Battle-in) before planning a purchase around a bonus card.

## Delta Reign ETB price, MSRP and availability

**US offers checked November 16, 2026:** Pokémon Center displayed $59.99 but marked its box **UNAVAILABLE**, with a purchase limit of two. A [TCGplayer regular-box listing](https://www.tcgplayer.com/product/712102/pokemon-me06-delta-reign-delta-reign-elite-trainer-box?Language=English) showed a featured **$84.98 offer with shipping included**. Compare the purchase quantity and seller conditions alongside the amount.

| Observed offer | Edition and purchase unit | Quoted amount | Condition and price type |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Pokémon Center | 1 Center ETB | $59.99 | Official-store price; unavailable; limit 2 |
| TCGplayer, Great Buys | 1 regular ETB | $84.98 | Advertised unopened offer; shipping included, before tax |
| TCGplayer, San Diego Dawg | Regular ETBs; minimum 3 | $80 each + $3.99 shipping shown | Seller minimum; orders below 3 cancelled |
| GameStop | 1 regular ETB | $99.99 | Retailer offer; condition/location availability checks |
| GameStop Pro | 1 regular ETB | $94.99 | Member offer; Pro required |
| TCGplayer case listing | Case described as 10 ETBs | $711.96 + $5 shipping | Seller asking price; confirm exact case unit |

### Can I buy one ETB at the $80 headline price?

On the captured November 16 **Delta Reign ETB** listing, the **$80 headline offer required at least three boxes**. Its item subtotal therefore starts at **$240: 3 × $80**, before shipping and tax. If you want exactly one ETB, that offer fails the seller’s quantity condition before you compare delivery costs. The separate **$84.98 one-box offer** showed shipping included on the saved page.

| Your buying task | Does the $80 seller’s quantity condition fit? | Amount you can establish from the captured row |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly one ETB | No; the seller requires at least three | No valid one-box checkout amount from that offer |
| At least three ETBs | The minimum quantity is met | Three boxes have a $240 item subtotal; verify shipping and tax at checkout |

The row displayed a shipping figure, but shipping for an actual three-box cart was not observed. Enter the delivery amount for your chosen quantity when comparing totals.

Keep the price labels with the numbers. The $59.99 is the Center official-store price; the other rows are seller or retailer offers. These sources do not establish a separate official **standard ETB MSRP**. Pack-count division compares bundle costs, not the value of cards you will pull.

## How should you compare a Delta Reign ETB case?

A single ETB and an ETB case are different sale units. The [TCGplayer English case listing](https://www.tcgplayer.com/product/712103/pokemon-me06-delta-reign-delta-reign-elite-trainer-box-case?Language=English) describes **10 Elite Trainer Boxes**. On November 16, it showed one unopened offer at **$711.96 plus $5 shipping**. That is a seller’s asking price. The same page showed **$793.07 Market Price**, **$716.95 Most Recent Sale** and **$825 Listed Median**; those are different price measures, not interchangeable checkout offers.

For that advertised offer and its stated quantity:

**($711.96 + $5 shipping) ÷ 10 ETBs = about $71.70 per ETB before tax.**

### Does a lower price per box fit your budget?

For a **$100 Delta Reign ETB order budget**, the observed **$716.96 case** and the **$240 three-box goods subtotal** already exceed the budget before any unknown costs. The $84.98 single-box offer leaves **$15.02 for tax or other checkout charges**. That headroom is a calculation, not a guarantee that the final order stays under $100.

Use this order of checks: **required edition → minimum boxes → whole-order cost → budget → cost per box or included pack**. A case can have a lower unit cost while requiring much more cash. The price-per-pack figure divides a complete ETB bundle, including its promos and accessories; it does not predict the cards you will pull or assign the whole price to loose booster packs.

### Compare an ETB quote with your quantity and budget

Enter the edition, desired number of boxes and an optional total budget. Choose a saved quote or use your own confirmed quote. For a case, enter the number of boxes in that seller's sale unit. Add the seller's minimum quantity, shipping for the **whole computed order**, and checkout tax when you know it.

The calculator rounds the purchase quantity up to the required whole boxes or cases. It then shows the **actual boxes ordered, whole-order amount, extra boxes, and cost per box and included pack**. Blank shipping or tax stays unknown. An unavailable product or unmet membership condition remains visible beside the arithmetic.

Confirm the seller’s exact case quantity and edition before ordering. The page’s individual-box accessory copy conflicts with the product descriptions used above, so use the edition table for contents rather than treating its generic copy as a new specification. This ten-box calculation applies to that listing. Compare the delivered amount per box, then the packs and promos in each box, when deciding between an ETB case and individual boxes.

## Has Delta Reign released, or is this a preorder?

**Delta Reign launched on November 6, 2026.** The official announcement included Elite Trainer Boxes among its release products. A store can still have an old preorder label, no stock or a later shipping allocation after the expansion launches. For a purchase now, read the store’s current fulfillment terms and expected shipping date as well as the expansion’s release date.

## Should you buy an ETB, packs or the single card?

Start with the result you want. An ETB bundles pack opening, its stated promo and play accessories. If you want a specific Kyogre promo, compare that exact edition and stamp with an identified single-card listing. Extra packs do not guarantee a particular chase card. For the expansion itself, use the [Delta Reign cards and release guide](/blog/delta-reign-pokemon).

After opening, match a physical pull’s set, full number, language and finish before checking its price. The [Pokémon card scanner](/pokemon-card-scanner) and [Pokémon catalog](/games/pokemon) help review supported records. Delta Reign’s public set currently has no single-card rows, so an older Rayquaza quote is not a Delta Reign value. Keep your sealed-box purchase comparison separate from the value of a specific pull.

paragraphs.question: What happened when we submitted Gengar?
paragraphs.draft:
In our **Pokémillion Daily check on November 16, 2026**, we submitted **Gengar** to a prompt asking for a Pokémon whose name begins with **G**. The game returned **Poké Ball / Common** and added **10 metres**. We completed that Daily with no answers submitted for the other six prompts; their result rows showed 0 m, and the final distance was 10 m.

| Recorded part of the Daily | Observation |
|---|---|
| First prompt condition | A Pokémon name beginning with G |
| Answer submitted | Gengar |
| Displayed result | Poké Ball / Common, +10 m |
| Remaining six prompts | No answers submitted; 0 m in their result rows |
| Final distance | 10 m |

The same result screen displayed a **Pelipper catch, marked Uncommon**, and **Pokédex progress of 1/1025** for this run. The record covers one submitted answer and completion of that dated Daily.

In our **Pokémillion Daily check on November 16, 2026**, we submitted **Gengar** to a prompt asking for a Pokémon whose name begins with **G**. |---|---|

| Answer submitted | Gengar |

| Final distance | 10 m |

page_plans.draft_markdown:
## What is Pokémillion, and where can you play?

Pokémillion is a fan-made Pokémon quiz with **seven encounters and 20 seconds for each encounter**. You name a Pokémon that fits the prompt, and less familiar valid answers can earn more distance. Play at [pokemillion.com](https://pokemillion.com/); this guide explains the rules and helps you distinguish the quiz from similarly named card-shopping results.

The useful distinction is between knowing a correct answer and finding an uncommon correct answer. A familiar Pokémon may satisfy a prompt but earn less distance. That makes the quiz different from a test in which every correct answer receives the same score. The official homepage already explains the core rules; the sections below separate the decisions you need to make while playing.

## Start with the prompt, then choose an answer

On the observed first-visit screen, the site asks you to select a trainer: Red Cap or Pink Cap. Its main menu then offers Daily Encounter and Unlimited Encounter. Choose the mode you intend to use, read the encounter’s condition, and name a Pokémon that matches it. The 20-second allowance applies to each encounter, rather than to all seven combined.

Under time pressure, first identify what the question tests. A type condition, an ability condition and an evolution condition ask for different things. Keep a valid answer in mind before trying to recall a less familiar one. This is a suggested approach, rather than a tested route to a particular score. The homepage says capitalization and typos do not matter, so matching the prompt is more useful than spending the timer adjusting letter case.

### What happened when we submitted Gengar?

In our **Pokémillion Daily check on November 16, 2026**, we submitted **Gengar** to a prompt asking for a Pokémon whose name begins with **G**. The game returned **Poké Ball / Common** and added **10 metres**. We completed that Daily with no answers submitted for the other six prompts; their result rows showed 0 m, and the final distance was 10 m.

| Recorded part of the Daily | Observation |
|---|---|
| First prompt condition | A Pokémon name beginning with G |
| Answer submitted | Gengar |
| Displayed result | Poké Ball / Common, +10 m |
| Remaining six prompts | No answers submitted; 0 m in their result rows |
| Final distance | 10 m |

The same result screen displayed a **Pelipper catch, marked Uncommon**, and **Pokédex progress of 1/1025** for this run. The record covers one submitted answer and completion of that dated Daily.

## Correctness and rarity are two separate checks

The game says its answer lists come from PokéAPI data covering types, forms, abilities, moves, evolutions and games. This is the eligibility check: does the answer belong to the list for that prompt? Read conditions about forms and other attributes carefully. A fact about one form or one game does not automatically establish that every version of the Pokémon satisfies the same condition.

Rarity is a separate familiarity ranking. For the best-known Pokémon, the site uses Google Trends data. For the rest, it describes a proxy based on games appeared in, fully evolved status and legendary status. It does not describe rarity as a live count of how many other players chose your answer, or as a literal count of words across the web. You cannot turn a tier label into an exact selection probability.

The homepage also says answers outside its lists on curated prompts can receive a live AI check. That describes a possible validation step. It does not mean every answer receives an AI score, or that AI replaces all of the underlying lists.

## What the six ball tiers add to your distance

The official homepage lists the following distance awards. “Common answers get you nowhere” is its slogan; the numerical table gives Common an award of **10 metres**, rather than zero.

| Ball tier | Rarity label | Distance added |
|---|---|---:|
| Poké Ball | Common | 10 m |
| Great Ball | Uncommon | 63 m |
| Ultra Ball | Rare | 160 m |
| Premier Ball | Epic | 360 m |
| Luxury Ball | Legendary | 640 m |
| Master Ball | One in a Pokémillion | 1,000 m |

These are game distances. “Legendary” in this table names a score tier; read it separately from the legendary-status attribute used in the familiarity proxy. Likewise, “One in a Pokémillion” is the displayed Master Ball label. The rules do not establish a one-in-a-million chance of receiving that tier. None of these distances measures a trading card’s value, condition or booster-pack pull rate.

## How to think about a rare answer

Use a two-step decision: **does it fit, and how familiar might it be?** An obscure name helps only if it satisfies the actual condition. Work from your knowledge of the requested attribute, then consider less obvious members of that group. For a form-specific question, check which form the prompt means before relying on a fact remembered about the species in general.

### How do I read the result comparison and answer tiers?

Read the comparison caption on a **Pokémillion** result before interpreting its percentage. Our 10 m result displayed **“Better than 1% of trainers”**; the caption identified the reference group as **simulated trainers on those prompts**. Use that number as the game’s simulated comparison for the run.

We also expanded the G-name prompt on the results screen to inspect its answer tiers. Its displayed Master Ball group included **Guzzlord** and **Great Tusk**, while **Gengar** appeared in the Poké Ball group. Those were the result screen’s examples for that prompt. Gengar was the only answer we submitted in the run. After a Daily, open the result for the specific prompt you want to review and read the displayed examples in that prompt’s context.

## Is Pokémillion free, and what does Unlimited mean?

The official game description calls Daily Encounter free, and the homepage says finishing one starts a daily streak. The [official Unlimited page](https://pokemillion.com/unlimitedPurchasepage) lists **US$5 as a one-time payment, with no subscription**, observed on 16 November 2026. It says checkout supports payment in your own currency. Unlimited lets you start a new run whenever you want and advertises no ads anywhere in the game.

### Which midnight does the Daily completion hint mean?

After we completed the **Pokémillion Daily**, the streak display changed from **0 days to 1 day**, and the menu marked that day’s encounter as finished. Its completion hint referred to **midnight in New York**. When reading that hint, use the named New York timezone rather than assuming it means midnight on your device’s local clock. This is the completion message recorded for the November 16 Daily.

The paid option also lists a stats tab for best distance and collected balls, Pokémon catches after each run, and future questions and updates. Choose it for additional runs and those features; Daily is the free route. The purchase page displays “Have a tester code?” but publishes no working code in the material reviewed. A related search for a code is not evidence of an active public offer. Check the game's current access details before paying, especially if account or cross-device access matters to you.

## Pokemillion or Pokemillon: check the destination

### Which site matches what I want to do?

Choose the destination by your task. **pokemillion.com**, with “million”, hosts the quiz. **pokemillon.com**, with “millon”, is a Spanish-language trading-card store. The observed U.S. search results and related queries mixed the spellings, so read the full domain before opening a result.

| What you want to do | Destination | What to check there |
|---|---|---|
| Play the Pokémon quiz | [pokemillion.com](https://pokemillion.com/) | Daily Encounter or the game’s Unlimited option |
| Read how the quiz judges answers | This guide and the game’s published rules | Prompt eligibility, familiarity and distance tiers |
| Buy physical cards or check a merchant order | [pokemillon.com](https://www.pokemillon.com/) | The merchant’s product, order and contact terms |

The guide supplies an explanation and the correct destinations. Orders and paid game access are handled by the respective external sites.

Use the game’s own site to play or check its access options. If you intended to shop for physical cards, follow the merchant destination and its terms instead. A quiz guide cannot verify a shop order or provide a playable encounter. The game also identifies itself as fan-made and unaffiliated with Krillion, Nintendo or The Pokémon Company.

content_changes.heading: What is Pokémillion, and where can you play?
content_changes.increment: 更快地回答对象与真实目的地；官方已完整说明基础机制，因此不把这段计为独家。
content_changes.gain_quote: Pokémillion is a fan-made Pokémon quiz with **seven encounters and 20 seconds for each encounter**. You name a Pokémon that fits the prompt, and less familiar valid answers can earn more distance. Play at [pokemillion.com](https://pokemillion.com/); this guide explains the rules and helps you distinguish the quiz from similarly named card-shopping results.

You name a Pokémon that fits the prompt, and less familiar valid answers can earn more distance. Play at [pokemillion.com](https://pokemillion.com/); this guide explains the rules and helps you distinguish the quiz from similarly named card-shopping results.

content_changes.heading: Which site matches what I want to do?
content_changes.increment: 把两个实际域名和用户任务做明确路由，减少错进商店/游戏的步骤；不构成新增可玩服务。
content_changes.gain_quote: Choose the destination by your task. **pokemillion.com**, with “million”, hosts the quiz. **pokemillon.com**, with “millon”, is a Spanish-language trading-card store. content_changes.text:
Choose the destination by your task. **pokemillion.com**, with “million”, hosts the quiz. **pokemillon.com**, with “millon”, is a Spanish-language trading-card store. The observed U.S. search results and related queries mixed the spellings, so read the full domain before opening a result.

| What you want to do | Destination | What to check there |
|---|---|---|
| Play the Pokémon quiz | [pokemillion.com](https://pokemillion.com/) | Daily Encounter or the game’s Unlimited option |

content_changes.heading: What happened when we submitted Gengar?
content_changes.increment: 提供一次真实免费Daily的题目条件、实际提交和返回值；将六题未提交与错误答案区分。
content_changes.gain_quote: In our **Pokémillion Daily check on November 16, 2026**, we submitted **Gengar** to a prompt asking for a Pokémon whose name begins with **G**. The game returned **Poké Ball / Common** and added **10 metres**. We completed that Daily with no answers submitted for the other six prompts; their result rows showed 0 m, and the final distance was 10 m.
content_changes.text:
In our **Pokémillion Daily check on November 16, 2026**, we submitted **Gengar** to a prompt asking for a Pokémon whose name begins with **G**. The game returned **Poké Ball / Common** and added **10 metres**. We completed that Daily with no answers submitted for the other six prompts; their result rows showed 0 m, and the final distance was 10 m.

| Recorded part of the Daily | Observation |
|---|---|
| First prompt condition | A Pokémon name beginning with G |
| Answer submitted | Gengar |
| Displayed result | Poké Ball / Common, +10 m |
| Remaining six prompts | No answers submitted; 0 m in their result rows |
| Final distance | 10 m |

The same result screen displayed a **Pelipper catch, marked Uncommon**, and **Pokédex progress of 1/1025** for this run. The record covers one submitted answer and completion of that dated Daily.
content_changes.scope_limit: 不是7题全部实际作答、识别准确率、提分对照或随机捕获分布实验。

content_changes.heading: How do I read the result comparison and answer tiers?
content_changes.increment: 公开结果caption的模拟比较口径，并用真实展开的每题tier表说明怎样复盘；不把显示的候选写成已提交验证。
content_changes.gain_quote: Read the comparison caption on a **Pokémillion** result before interpreting its percentage. Our 10 m result displayed **“Better than 1% of trainers”**; the caption identified the reference group as **simulated trainers on those prompts**. Use that number as the game’s simulated comparison for the run.
content_changes.text:
Read the comparison caption on a **Pokémillion** result before interpreting its percentage. Our 10 m result displayed **“Better than 1% of trainers”**; the caption identified the reference group as **simulated trainers on those prompts**. Use that number as the game’s simulated comparison for the run.

We also expanded the G-name prompt on the results screen to inspect its answer tiers. Its displayed Master Ball group included **Guzzlord** and **Great Tusk**, while **Gengar** appeared in the Poké Ball group. Those were the result screen’s examples for that prompt. Gengar was the only answer we submitted in the run. After a Daily, open the result for the specific prompt you want to review and read the displayed examples in that prompt’s context.
content_changes.scope_limit: 1%不是实际玩家排名。Guzzlord/GreatTusk未提交，不能写成实测满分、固定每日答案、每种题都有效的策略或全物种通用评分表。

content_changes.heading: Which midnight does the Daily completion hint mean?
content_changes.increment: 补出真实完成后界面命名的NewYork时区和streak状态，避免默认读者本地午夜。
content_changes.gain_quote: After we completed the **Pokémillion Daily**, the streak display changed from **0 days to 1 day**, and the menu marked that day’s encounter as finished. Its completion hint referred to **midnight in New York**. When reading that hint, use the named New York timezone rather than assuming it means midnight on your device’s local clock. This is the completion message recorded for the November 16 Daily.

changes.heading: Which contents should I use when product listings disagree?
changes.increment: 逐字段展示已捕获卖家generic文案与制造商的差异，按具体版本确定取值；这是一项网页来源核对，不是开箱。
changes.gain_quote: For the **Delta Reign ETB**, use the manufacturer’s description for the exact edition. In our November 16 page check, Pokémon’s standard-box showcase listed **40 Energy cards and a plastic coin**. The TCGplayer standard-box description listed **45 Energy cards and two plastic condition markers**. These are different descriptions, so we keep the manufacturer’s standard-box specification in the contents table.
changes.text:
For the **Delta Reign ETB**, use the manufacturer’s description for the exact edition. In our November 16 page check, Pokémon’s standard-box showcase listed **40 Energy cards and a plastic coin**. The TCGplayer standard-box description listed **45 Energy cards and two plastic condition markers**. These are different descriptions, so we keep the manufacturer’s standard-box specification in the contents table.

| Field checked | Manufacturer’s standard-box description | Marketplace description captured |
|---|---|---|
| Energy cards | 40 | 45 |
| Play-accessory wording | Plastic coin | Two plastic condition markers |

changes.heading: Can I buy one ETB at the $80 headline price?
changes.increment: 将卖家最少3盒条件换算为240商品小计，再按用户要1盒或至少3盒作可行性判断。
changes.gain_quote: On the captured November 16 **Delta Reign ETB** listing, the **$80 headline offer required at least three boxes**. Its item subtotal therefore starts at **$240: 3 × $80**, before shipping and tax. If you want exactly one ETB, that offer fails the seller’s quantity condition before you compare delivery costs. The separate **$84.98 one-box offer** showed shipping included on the saved page.
changes.text:
On the captured November 16 **Delta Reign ETB** listing, the **$80 headline offer required at least three boxes**. Its item subtotal therefore starts at **$240: 3 × $80**, before shipping and tax. If you want exactly one ETB, that offer fails the seller’s quantity condition before you compare delivery costs. The separate **$84.98 one-box offer** showed shipping included on the saved page.

| Your buying task | Does the $80 seller’s quantity condition fit? | Amount you can establish from the captured row |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly one ETB | No; the seller requires at least three | No valid one-box checkout amount from that offer |
| At least three ETBs | The minimum quantity is met | Three boxes have a $240 item subtotal; verify shipping and tax at checkout |

The row displayed a shipping figure, but shipping for an actual three-box cart was not observed. Enter the delivery amount for your chosen quantity when comparing totals.
scope_limit: 三盒购物车的实际shipping/tax与库存未读；不能将3.99自动视为三盒整单固定费用，也不能称243.99为已验证结账总价。

changes.heading: Does a lower price per box fit your budget?
changes.increment: 给出预算判定顺序，避免以单位价推荐超出预算的大订单。
changes.gain_quote: For a **$100 Delta Reign ETB order budget**, the observed **$716.96 case** and the **$240 three-box goods subtotal** already exceed the budget before any unknown costs. The $84.98 single-box offer leaves **$15.02 for tax or other checkout charges**. That headroom is a calculation, not a guarantee that the final order stays under $100.
changes.text:
For a **$100 Delta Reign ETB order budget**, the observed **$716.96 case** and the **$240 three-box goods subtotal** already exceed the budget before any unknown costs. The $84.98 single-box offer leaves **$15.02 for tax or other checkout charges**. That headroom is a calculation, not a guarantee that the final order stays under $100.

Use this order of checks: **required edition → minimum boxes → whole-order cost → budget → cost per box or included pack**. A case can have a lower unit cost while requiring much more cash. The price-per-pack figure divides a complete ETB bundle, including its promos and accessories; it does not predict the cards you will pull or assign the whole price to loose booster packs.

changes.heading: Compare an ETB quote with your quantity and budget
changes.increment: 本地HTML中实际接收数量/预算/报价，给订单资金需求、单位价和未知费用；官网集成另需实施。

For a case, enter the number of boxes in that seller's sale unit. Add the seller's minimum quantity, shipping for the **whole computed order**, and checkout tax when you know it.
changes.text:
Enter the edition, desired number of boxes and an optional total budget. Choose a saved quote or use your own confirmed quote. For a case, enter the number of boxes in that seller's sale unit. Add the seller's minimum quantity, shipping for the **whole computed order**, and checkout tax when you know it.

The calculator rounds the purchase quantity up to the required whole boxes or cases. It then shows the **actual boxes ordered, whole-order amount, extra boxes, and cost per box and included pack**. Blank shipping or tax stays unknown. An unavailable product or unmet membership condition remains visible beside the arithmetic.

changes.text:
Read the comparison caption on a **Pokémillion** result before interpreting its percentage. Our 10 m result displayed **“Better than 1% of trainers”**; the caption identified the reference group as **simulated trainers on those prompts**. Use that number as the game’s simulated comparison for the run.

We also expanded the G-name prompt on the results screen to inspect its answer tiers. Its displayed Master Ball group included **Guzzlord** and **Great Tusk**, while **Gengar** appeared in the Poké Ball group. Those were the result screen’s examples for that prompt. Gengar was the only answer we submitted in the run. After a Daily, open the result for the specific prompt you want to review and read the displayed examples in that prompt’s context.
